options.text: Their feet are different lengths, so the same blackboard gives different counts.
A body unit that is not the same for every student can produce different numbers for one length.
The blackboard itself changed length between the two measurements.
Only Ojas measured correctly because a larger count always means a better measurement.

stem:
Ojas and Bilal measure the same classroom blackboard along its bottom edge using their own foot-lengths. Ojas gets 9 foot-lengths. Bilal gets 7 foot-lengths.

Which claims correctly explain why the numbers differ? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Different body units (foot-lengths) give different counts for the same length. The board did not change, and a larger count is not automatically better.
